intro: Pick the best one. Hints are here if you want them.

items.stem: Which one explains the evidence from Document 1?

options.1: This shows R. R. Palmer and other historians wrote A History of the Modern World, a textbook about the past
options.2: This shows farming has been an important way of life in Britain for a very long time, hundreds of years
options.3: This shows landowners ran Parliament, which matters because they could pass the enclosure acts that remade farming
options.4: This shows that from 1688 to 1832 the British government was mostly in the hands of the landowners

hints: One of these says the document again in different words.
items.reason: Option 4 repeats the document. Option 1 explains the source line. Option 2 is true and explains nothing. Only option 3 says what the evidence shows and why it matters.

items.stem: Which one explains the evidence from Document 4?

options.1: This shows Baines said the island location and the command of the seas kept England safe from invasion
options.2: This shows Edward Baines wrote a history of cotton manufacture and compared England with other countries
options.3: This shows many countries in Europe fought wars against each other in the 1700s and the early 1800s
options.4: This shows England was safe from invasion, which matters because owners could build factories without war at home

hints: Which one gets past what Baines said and onto what it meant?
Only one of these could help you answer why it started in Britain.
items.reason: Option 1 is Baines again. Option 2 is about the author, not the evidence. Option 3 is about Europe, not this document. Option 4 names the consequence and ties it to factories.

items.stem: Your claim is that new machines and new power changed how goods were made. Which explanation ties Document 8 back to it?

options.1: This shows steam engines raised the coal that fed more engines, which matters because factories no longer needed a river
options.2: This shows Andrew Ure wrote The Philosophy of Manufactures, a book about the factory system of Great Britain
options.3: This shows Ure wrote that steam engines lend their powerful arms to drain the pits and to raise the coals
options.4: This shows steam engines were one of the most important inventions in history and are still studied today

hints: Two of these are about the book or its words, not what they mean.
Which one says something about how goods were made?
items.reason: Option 2 is the source line. Option 3 quotes the document back. Option 4 is a general opinion. Option 1 says what the evidence shows and why it changed where factories could be built.
